I think it's okay, but if I'm to be honest with you; you're better off just getting Sniper Elite 5 if you haven't already, in my personal opinion the maps are better in 5, it's cheaper and usually goes on sale for much less than this game considering this game is "new" (I use the term "new" lightly because this game really feels like Sniper Elite 5 but with a worse-to-same roster of guns and a different protagonist, who mind you, was a side character from 5, and different maps, which I personally don't feel are much better than 5's and also re-use a lot of assets from 5, not to mention how when it comes to invasions; some scenarios are heavily stacked against you due to map design, as if the odds weren't already stacked against you while invading a host with focus mode and whatnot) 

Haven't played much of the multiplayer or survival since I was never a big fan of either in Sniper Elite 5 so I didn't think I would be here either, tried both, still not my cup of tea, not to mention they seemingly still have hackers and cheaters despite the new anti-cheat, so expect more of the same in that regard, but from a mostly campaign / invasion stand-point, this game just feels like Sniper Elite 5.2 with not enough new additions to warrant the higher price-tag, not to mention locking some of the guns they copy & pasted from Sniper Elite 5 into this game behind a pay-wall like the Kar98k and M1911 which are pretty iconic and some of my favourite guns ever which feels really bad to have to buy as DLC if you actually want them like me. If I had any recommendation for a way to play if you really want to play this game specifically and not just Sniper Elite 5 for some reason; I'd say give it a go on game-pass and see how you feel considering it would be cheaper on your wallet, just personally don't think this game is worth the price unless it's on a deeper sale (I only got this on a 25% off sale, hardly justifiable to me, but I'm a fool so I did it anyway, I'd urge you to not do the same)

TLDR; Just play Sniper Elite 5 instead, it'll be less buggy and probably a more enjoyable experience to you, if you already have, well, you're really not missing out on much, this isn't Sniper Elite 6.

[h1]Positive:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Very beautiful maps 
[*] Maps with enormous elevation differences
[*] Hidden locations where you can hide
[/list]

[h1]Negative:[/h1]
[list]
[*] The game is too easy – it is clearly aimed more at children/teenagers 
[*] The maps are too small – although larger than in, for example, SE4, the walkable areas are limited
[*] There are too few AI enemies – although on average 50% larger than in, for example, SE4, the number of AI enemies is roughly the same as in SE4 
[*] Too few objectives – with only 19 collectibles per map, the tasks are too limited
[*] Many locations on the maps are empty – empty buildings, nothing interesting to find
[/list]

All maps are very well designed. I like the graphics. Rebellion has once again shown: graphic design is something they do very well. Especially the latest DLC map from Season Pass 1, Angriffsreichweite, is in my opinion not only the most beautiful in this game but also the most beautiful map in the entire franchise. Clearly, they have really gone all out here: there are many elevation changes to overcome, numerous entry points into the central building complex, and just as many ways to get lost. Overall, this third DLC map is the best that Rebellion has delivered so far in the SE universe.

[h2]What Rebellion does very well:[/h2]
Graphic design. But that’s about all the positives.

[h2]What Rebellion cannot do: Game mechanics[/h2]
Because what Rebellion apparently does not master or repeatedly fails to deliver is good game mechanics. These are – repeatedly – as terrible as in SE5!

[list]
[*] In most maps, an invasion (my preferred game mode) can only take place after certain objectives are completed, areas reached, or enough attention has been generated. This often results in players clearing a map of AI soldiers—making it almost or completely empty—especially when playing co-op missions. As a result, the intruder (invader) operates alone against two players and is at a significant disadvantage. Many of my fellow players believe there’s no reason for this setup; invasion should be possible from the start to give the intruder a fair chance to defend themselves or act under cover of AI soldiers.

[*] Generally speaking, all maps have far too few AI enemies. Considering that the game’s theme revolves around fighting against the Wehrmacht—the armies that plunged the world into a devastating war—and that many maps focus on destroying facilities containing deadly weapon systems, factories, and logistical infrastructure, it’s almost laughable to have only about 130 AI enemies per map.

[*] When it comes to killing Hitler—the probably most dangerous man of his time—I wonder why his location is secured by only a maximum of 120 soldiers. Even an alarm trigger only summons a handful of soldiers, which isn’t much of a challenge for a player with some practice. This was already a flaw in SE5; it’s being repeated here. Also, that this man always hides in exactly the same building—a wooden hut with an open window—looks like developers decided early on that this should remain unchanged.

[*] Why isn’t it possible to increase difficulty by raising the expected number of soldiers?

[*] What’s stopping us from making the game genuinely harder for those who want it?

In my co-op games, I’ve often discussed this aspect. All players agree: It would make the game not only more interesting but also more valuable if there were options to play with higher difficulty levels and significantly more AI soldiers.

[/list]

[h2]Additional criticisms:[/h2]

[list]
[*] The AI stands bored around and doesn’t become active even when individual soldiers encounter bodies lying on the ground during patrols.

[*] Alarms are either not triggered or only very late and summon only a small number of soldiers who come out predictably from the same rooms and can often be taken out with just a few precise shots.

[*] Overall, it’s far too easy to memorize AI behavior and their locations—so you’re quickly prepared for what’s coming.

[*] At many points on new maps, it’s either possible or impossible to climb walls—whether through “grapevines” or simply jumping up—sometimes failing because climbing isn’t successful.

[*] On many parts of new maps, it’s impossible to shoot through wall parapets. We’ve long gotten used to not being able to shoot through glass or leaves—that was true in SE5 and remains so in SE:R—but not being able to shoot targets between parapets is ridiculous. It looks like programmers and graphic artists aren’t working together but rather against each other at these points—same goes for fences and railings.

[*] There are many spots where your character gets stuck because something blocks movement—you often don’t even see what it is until you back up and go around it. In attack or defense situations, this is more than just bad—it’s unacceptable.

[*] There seems to be no consistent rule about how high your character can jump from—sometimes jumping from several meters height isn’t an issue; other times falling onto concrete breaks bones as if falling from a much lower height. This was also criticized back in SE5.

[*] Regarding “old bugs”: A few weeks after SE5 was released, Rebellion claimed they fixed infinite reloading weapons bug—but now this problem seems extended from rifles to submachine guns and handguns as well. This flaw can be especially problematic during invasions.
[/list]

[h2]Conclusion:[/h2]
A game that can be completed quickly. Even at highest difficulty level for experienced players, unfortunately no real challenge.
A few glitches but fulfilling play.

Ehh, I regret this purchase, like other reviews said it could just be a DLC for SE5.
Buy the game on sale if you are interested in purchasing it. Otherwise stay clear

It feels more like a DLC for Sniper Elite 5 than a ful sequel. The gameplay and visuals are about 90% the same, right down to some of the bugs. If you enjoyed SE5, you will likely have fun with this too. On the other hand, it's hard to justify the 50€ price tag. At 30–40€, it is a fine expansion.
